purpose: Paliperidone palmitate is used to treat schizophrenia and, in some forms, schizoaffective disorder. It helps reduce symptoms like hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. It can also help prevent these symptoms from coming back over time.
how_it_works: This medication works by balancing certain chemical messengers in your brain, mainly dopamine and serotonin. When these chemicals are out of balance, they can cause symptoms like hearing or seeing things that aren't there, or having unusual beliefs. By steadying these brain chemicals, the medication helps you think more clearly and feel more stable.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include weight gain, feeling restless or having trouble sitting still, drowsiness, dizziness, increased blood sugar, injection site pain or redness, headache, and increased levels of a hormone called prolactin which can cause changes in menstrual periods or breast tenderness.
warnings: This medication is not recommended for elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis, as it can increase the risk of serious heart events or stroke. Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, diabetes, kidney disease, or seizures. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. It may cause a rare but serious movement disorder called tardive dyskinesia. Do not stop this medication without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an injection by a healthcare provider, not taken as a pill at home. Invega Sustenna is given once a month, Invega Trinza is given once every 3 months, and Invega Hafyera is given once every 6 months. Your doctor will decide the right dose and schedule based on your individual needs.
